data.heading: The same task, two very different results.
data.intro: One person asked AI for help. The other gave it a brief, the way you would brief a sharp new hire.

slides.title: A client proposal where AI interviews you
slides.before_prompt: write me a proposal for a new marketing project for a client thanks
slides.before_result: AI knows nothing about the client, so it guesses.
slides.after_prompt: I need to write a proposal for a client, but I want to make sure you have everything you need to draft it well. Before you start, ask me the five questions that would most improve the quality of your draft.
after_replies: What is the client's industry and size?
What specific problem are they trying to solve?
What is the project scope and budget range?
What is the timeline and key deliverable?
What has already been discussed or agreed with the client?
slides.after_result: AI asks first, so it has what it needs.

slides.title: A launch line nobody else would say
slides.before_prompt: give me three taglines for our launch deck something catchy
slides.before_result: Back came “Work Smarter, Not Harder.”
slides.after_prompt: Give me three opening lines a competitor would never dare to put on a slide, including one that's a little uncomfortable.
slides.after_result: One of the three became the deck's hook.

slides.title: Preparing for a meeting with the CFO
slides.before_prompt: got a stakeholder meeting coming up can you help me get ready for it
slides.before_result: “Stakeholder meeting” tells AI nothing useful.
slides.after_prompt: Act as an executive coach. I have a 30-minute meeting tomorrow with the VP of Operations and the CFO... I expect pushback on implementation timeline and switching costs. Help me prepare by generating... the two or three objections most likely to come up and a one-sentence response to each...
slides.after_result: AI is asked for the likely objections and an answer to each.

slides.title: A 40-page report for a VP with five minutes
slides.before_prompt: summarize this report whats important in it
slides.before_result: A summary that takes longer to read than it's worth.
slides.after_prompt: Act as a senior analyst who has just read this 40-page market research report. I need a summary for a VP who has five minutes to read it before a board meeting. She needs to understand: (1) the top three findings that have strategic implications for our industry, (2) any finding that contradicts our current assumptions, and (3) one question she should be ready to answer if asked. Format as a three-section briefing with headers. Under 300 words total.
slides.after_result: AI is asked for any finding that goes against your assumptions.

slides.title: When someone keeps missing deadlines
slides.before_prompt: need to talk to someone on my team about a problem what do i even say
slides.before_result: AI softens the message until the point is lost.
slides.after_prompt: Act as an executive coach... I need to speak with a team member who has been consistently missing deadlines. I've given informal feedback twice in the past two months, but nothing has changed... Do not script the full conversation...
slides.after_result: Now AI knows you've raised this twice already.

slides.title: Rewriting a weak paragraph
slides.before_prompt: make this better it doesnt sound right
slides.before_result: The changes are cosmetic and often miss what was wrong.
slides.after_prompt: Act as a copy editor for business non-fiction. Rewrite the following paragraph for clarity and impact... The current version is too hedged and too long. Tighten it to four sentences maximum... Flag any sentence where you're unsure whether the change preserves my meaning.
slides.after_result: Now AI knows what's wrong: too hedged and too long.

slides.title: Marketing a product with no audience yet
slides.before_prompt: write me a marketing plan cover all the bases
slides.before_result: AI goes broad and never gets specific.
slides.after_prompt: what would an experienced growth marketer consider before setting a budget for a product with no existing audience?
slides.after_result: The answer comes back precise, from an expert's point of view.

slides.title: Writing a performance review
slides.before_prompt: help me write a performance review for my direct report what should i put in it
slides.before_result: Flattering filler that you then have to strip out.
slides.after_prompt: Act as a manager writing an annual performance review for a mid-level marketing analyst. This person consistently produces accurate, high-quality work but rarely speaks up in meetings... The review will be used for compensation and promotion decisions... Do not use filler phrases like “team player” or “hard worker.”
slides.after_result: AI is told to skip “team player” and “hard worker.”

slides.title: Reading an employee survey
slides.before_prompt: can you go through this employee survey and tell me the main takeaways
slides.before_result: A list of what came up most often.
slides.after_prompt: Act as an organizational psychologist reviewing an internal employee engagement survey... Identify the top three patterns that suggest systemic issues rather than individual complaints... Do not make recommendations yet...
slides.after_result: AI is asked which problems come from how the company runs.

slides.title: Researching your competitors
slides.before_prompt: can you look into the competition for my business whats out there
slides.before_result: An overview of the big names you already know.
slides.after_prompt: Act as a market analyst. I need a competitive intelligence brief on the mid-market HR software category... I'm specifically looking for: pricing model trends in the past 18 months... Flag any claim where your training data may be outdated...
slides.after_result: AI is told to flag anything that may be out of date.

sections.note: 4. What you'll be able to do: the four parts as outcomes

data.heading: What you'll be able to do
data.intro: Read it in order once, then keep the back of the book open beside your work.

parts.label: Part 1
parts.outcome: Hand AI its first proper task this week, and know what happens when you type.
points: Why it felt like a gimmick, and the Mirror Principle (Ch 1)
The four fears that hold people back, and the way past each (Ch 2)
The Director's Mindset and the RTC framework: role, task, constraint (Ch 3)

parts.label: Part 2
parts.outcome: Pick one tool with confidence and know which mode suits each job.
points: Three questions that settle which tool to use (Ch 7)
Default, reasoning or creative mode, matched to the task (Ch 8, free to read)
Six hands-on exercises, starting with the email you've been avoiding (Ch 9)

parts.label: Part 3
parts.outcome: Fix a weak draft with one precise note, and catch an error before anyone else sees it.
points: The Three Fundamental Rules: be specific, ask for one thing, iterate (Ch 10)
The Diagnostic Ladder for fixing a draft that missed (Ch 11)
Two-Step Verification and a 3-month practice plan (Ch 13 and Ch 14)

parts.label: The appendices
parts.outcome: Reach for a written fix or a starting point whenever a prompt misfires or a new task lands.
points: Ten common failures, each with its corrective prompt
A quick reference card, a tool comparison and a plain-English glossary

items.q: Do I need a technical background?
items.a: None. The book is written for professionals with no technical training. If you can write an email, you can use everything in it.

items.q: Which AI tool does it use?
items.a: It works with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot. Part 2 helps you pick one, and the directing skill carries over to all of them.

items.q: Will it go out of date when the tools change?
items.a: The book teaches you how to direct AI, and that skill carries over from one model to the next. The product names will keep changing, and your briefs will keep working.

items.q: I already use AI at work. Is it still for me?
items.a: Yes, if your results are hit and miss. The frameworks turn scattered habits into a method you can repeat, and the appendices give you prompts and fixes to keep beside your work.
Kindle, paperback and hardcover are all on Amazon, with Amazon's standard returns. The paperback is handy to keep open beside your desk for the appendices.

items.q: Can I read some of it first?
items.a: Yes. Chapter 8 is free to read, and it shows you which AI mode fits which job.
